A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research and contain the main text and Appendices A–E. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable and matchable. v6 additionally includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original membership-inference experiments on fine-tuned image classifiers and fitted vulnerability models. Table A7 explicitly attributes several FiLM results to this work.

after.justification: v6 retains the original membership-inference experiments, regression results and individual-vulnerability analyses in Section 4 and Appendix D, including the results attributed to this work in Table A7.

M1.justification: The simplified class-mean model, LiRA/RMIA procedures, fine-tuning configurations and vulnerability-prediction models remain unchanged. The wording and vector-notation edits do not change their procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Patch Camelyon, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, EuroSAT, Pets and Resisc45 with the same task coverage. The added discussion of LLM pre-training cites another work and introduces no LLM experiment.

E2.justification: The LiRA/RMIA comparisons retain the same participants. Figure 5 and Table A7 also retain the same Head, FiLM and from-scratch target-model comparisons. No newly cited work becomes an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix C retain the experimental settings, including 256 shadow/reference models, 20 Optuna iterations and the 70/30 hyperparameter-tuning split. Evaluation metrics and the individual-vulnerability testing procedure are unchanged.

E4.justification: The dataset-property sensitivity, transfer across target models, individual-vulnerability and alternative-regression analyses are retained. Figure 6's added average-case curve and new Figure 7 redisplay analyses already reported in Sections 4.2–4.5 and Appendix E.

E5.justification: Six-seed and twelve-seed reporting, Clopper–Pearson intervals, min/max error bars and regression confidence intervals are retained. Checklist item 7 summarizes statistical practices already documented in v5.

E6.justification: The result tables and fitted coefficients are unchanged; Table A8 still reports training/test R2 of 0.930/0.790 at FPR 0.001. Figure 6 reuses average-case results from Figure 3, while Figure 7 illustrates the existing DP extrapolation rather than reporting new findings.

T1.justification: The mathematical statements and proof steps are retained. v6 identifies the existing He notation as Hermite polynomials after Equation A63 and standardizes boldface for class-mean vectors. These clarify notation without changing the derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the power-law claims for average and individual vulnerability, empirical support in transfer learning, and the extremely large dataset sizes predicted for protecting the most vulnerable samples.

C2.justification: Remark 3 replaces the broad expectation against similar power laws in general training algorithms with explicit uncertainty about convergence and its rate for larger networks trained from scratch. Section 4.3 reinforces the simplified-model qualification. Section 5 adds LLM pre-training as a promising but computationally expensive extension.

D1.justification: The new checklist states that documented source code and reproduction instructions accompany the supplementary material. This adds access/documentation information; Appendix C's implementation settings, hardware descriptions and existing public repository link remain unchanged. An actual new code release is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v6 adds Hayes et al. (2025) and briefly relates its LLM pre-training study to LiRA vulnerability and dataset size. The Azize and Basu citation changes from preprint to publication metadata for the same work.

P1.justification: v6 makes localized spelling, punctuation and prose edits, explains the Hermite-polynomial notation, and appends a NeurIPS checklist. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 6 gains the existing average-case curve, a wider logarithmic y-range and an expanded caption. New Figure 7 visualizes the existing average/worst-case DP extrapolation. Nearby figures, tables and text are repositioned; the appendix result displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v6 makes the existing evidence easier to interpret through Figure 6's direct average/individual comparison and Figure 7's DP-extrapolation illustration. Remark 3 more carefully expresses uncertainty beyond the simplified model, and the Hermite notation is clarified. These provide limited gains in clarity and qualification while the empirical evidence and central conclusions remain unchanged.
